# Pinned upstream evaluator

This private Lucid-compatible WebAssembly package uses the unmodified published
`uplc 1.1.23` crate. [Aiken PR #1355](https://github.com/aiken-lang/aiken/pull/1355)
added protocol-aware evaluation and extended cost-model parsing. The earlier
local patch to `uplc 1.1.22` is removed. Cargo verifies the published source
against the checksum in `rust/Cargo.lock`.

Offchain Lucid `0.4.29` and Gateway Lucid `0.4.34` do not pass a protocol
version to their embedded evaluator.
Upstream `1.1.23` defaults to protocol 11 semantics when no version is supplied.
Our compatible `eval_phase_two_raw` entrypoint therefore explicitly selects
**protocol 10**, the bridge's supported local evaluation profile. It forwards
all costs, budgets and scripts unchanged. It never selects a protocol from the
number of cost parameters. A 350-entry table does not establish protocol-11
acceptance.

The additional `eval_phase_two_raw_with_protocol` entrypoint permits explicit
versions 9 through 11 and rejects other versions. Current Lucid does not call
it. Automatic selection from live ledger parameters and bridge qualification
for protocol 11 remain separate work. Production provider evaluation uses the
node's protocol selection. Do not use Lucid's versionless local evaluation on
another protocol and assume that its estimates establish ledger acceptance.

Both Gateway (npm override) and offchain (Deno link and locked transitive
resolution) use these artifacts. The local package version is `0.2.23+ibc.2`,
not an upstream npm release. The package override is still required until Lucid
publishes a compatible evaluator. Updating the Aiken compiler alone does not
replace it. Keep the direct Deno dependency and linked transitive resolutions.

Build with Rust 1.97.1, wasm-pack 0.13.1 and LLVM clang 20.1.8. On macOS use
Homebrew LLVM rather than Apple's clang, which lacks the WebAssembly target:

```sh
CC_wasm32_unknown_unknown=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/clang \
  python3 cardano/vendor/uplc/build.py
node cardano/vendor/uplc/verify.cjs
```

The default build compares every generated byte with `artifact-sha256.json`.
Use `--write` only when intentionally updating and reviewing the artifacts.
`rust/Cargo.lock` pins all Rust dependencies. Different compiler versions may
produce different bytes and must not silently replace the recorded artifacts.

`deno task test:deployment` includes real WASM regressions for 297- and 350-entry
bitwise costs and a valid Unicode script whose cost distinguishes protocol 10
from 11. It also checks that Lucid and utils load the recorded artifacts. The
consensus-history, packet-budget and migration suites exercise actual compiled
bridge validators. See `docs/migration-implementation-evidence.md` for results.
